h: Smart Moves for a London Round
p: Group bookings are where crazy golf really shines. If your gang is large, ask about group options when you book, work out smaller teams before you arrive and make it a contest. A losers-buy-the-next-round rule tends to focus the mind, though a forfeit like singing on the walk to dinner is cheaper.

Arrive a little early so you can grab a drink and settle in rather than rushing straight to the first hole. London is busy on weeknights as well as weekends, so leave plenty of time for travel, especially if you're coming across town on the Tube during rush hour.

If you're planning a bigger day around your round, London's free museums are a great way to start. The Natural History Museum, the Science Museum and the British Museum all cost nothing to enter for their main collections, and Tate Modern on the South Bank is packed with modern art. Borough Market, near London Bridge, is a foodie haven for an afternoon graze.

For a bit of fresh air, the parks are hard to beat. Hyde Park, Regent's Park and Greenwich Park all offer room to roam, and a stroll along the Thames from Westminster to Tower Bridge takes in many of the capital's most famous sights. Finish with your round and you've got a properly full London day.
